dedupe_keys.name: easy simauto esa python automation for powerworld simulator

description: Easy SimAuto (ESA) is a Python package that makes it easy to automate PowerWorld Simulator, a commercial power system analysis program, through its Simulator Automation Server (SimAuto). It was created by Brandon Thayer, Zeyu Mao, Yijing Liu, Katherine Davis and Thomas Overbye and described in the Journal of Open Source Software in 2020, to spare researchers the awkward low-level interface. ESA wraps all SimAuto functions, supports PowerWorld auxiliary scripts, adds helper functions, returns data as Pandas data frames wherever possible, and adds native implementations of recent algorithms. The project reports full test coverage and documentation. Coverage is not tied to a place. The package is accessible on GitHub and installable from PyPI under the Apache 2.0 licence at no cost, with earlier Zenodo archives under MIT, 27 tags and a latest commit in December 2025. Caveats: it needs a licensed PowerWorld Simulator with SimAuto, so it cannot run on its own. Simulation uses are scripting power flow, contingency and large synthetic grid studies. Related records: data-tamu-electric-grid-test-cases provides grid cases in PowerWorld format.
